metadata.title: The Best Fix for a Biased Model Didn't Touch the Model
metadata.topic: BIAS & FAIRNESS · CAUSAL PATHS & LEVERAGE ANALYSIS
metadata.purpose: Answer one real question in the Plain register: why does the best fix for a biased AI often leave the model untouched? Lands the carry-out that an intervention only removes what its causal path carries, and the highest-leverage path often bypasses the model entirely.
metadata.anchor_pair: B06 -> B07 (Causal path diagram from world to outcome with bias flowing through it; interventions as dams)
metadata.one_flag: B10 — qualitative leverage at deployment does not mean the model is blameless

beats.narration_text: When an AI system produces biased outcomes, engineers reflexively fix the code or retrain the model. But the fix that actually works often leaves the model completely untouched. Let's trace why.

shot.new_visual_element: Writer types naive question, hesitates on "retraining the model", corrects to "looking outside the model"

props.text:
If an AI model is producing biased outcomes,
shouldn't we fix it by
retraining the model?

beats.note: B00 is Remotion (BrutalistHesitantWriter) per course-skepticism SKILL.md. Liam reads over typing animation.

beats.narration_text: Consider a constructed case from real practice. A deployed AI pipeline produces documented disparities in downstream decisions. Three engineering teams are given the exact same mission: eliminate the disparity.

shot.new_visual_element: Constructed Composite Case: Deployed AI Decision Pipeline with Disparate Outcomes across groups

production_viz.label: Constructed Case: Deployed Decision Pipeline
production_viz.mechanic: Pipeline card showing documented disparities in real-world decisions. Explicitly flagged as constructed composite.

beats.narration_text: The first team rewrites the loss function. They add an algorithmic penalty to punish disparate group error rates and retrain. The disparity drops slightly, but mostly persists.

shot.new_visual_element: Team One: Loss Function Penalty Added -> Retrained Model -> Marginal Disparity Drop

production_viz.label: Team 1: In-Model Loss Penalty
production_viz.mechanic: Intervention 1: Loss rewritten with fairness penalty term. Outcome: Disparity drops slightly; problem largely unchanged.

beats.narration_text: The second team rebuilds the training data. They recruit underrepresented groups, rebalance the dataset, and retrain the original model. The disparity shifts shape, but the core imbalance remains.

shot.new_visual_element: Team Two: Training Dataset Rebalanced -> Subgroups Expanded -> Disparity Reshaped but Persistent

production_viz.label: Team 2: Data Resampling
production_viz.mechanic: Intervention 2: Underrepresented cohorts sampled; dataset rebalanced. Outcome: Disparity changes shape; imbalance persists.

beats.narration_text: The third team touches neither the model nor the training data. Instead, they examine the room the model was deployed into: downstream human review and decision thresholds. The disparity collapses by an order of magnitude.

shot.new_visual_element: Team Three: Deployment Context & Review Room Restructured -> Order of Magnitude Reduction

production_viz.label: Team 3: Deployment Room Intervention
production_viz.mechanic: Intervention 3: Human review room and decision thresholds re-architected; model untouched. Outcome: Disparity drops by order of magnitude.

beats.narration_text: Teams one and two were not incompetent. Their fixes were genuine, but low leverage. They acted on real causal paths that happened to carry very little of the bias.

shot.new_visual_element: Three Interventions Compared: Real causal paths vs Low-leverage vs High-leverage

production_viz.label: The Three Teams Puzzle
production_viz.mechanic: Comparison showing that honesty and technical competence do not equal high leverage if the path carries little flow.

beats.narration_text: To see why, draw the causal path from the world to the final decision. The protected attribute feeds proxy features, which split: some enter the model, but others bypass it directly into human review.

shot.new_visual_element: Causal Path Diagram: Protected Attribute -> Proxies -> Model Inputs vs Bypass Channels -> Downstream Review -> Decision

production_viz.label: The Causal Path Network
production_viz.mechanic: Visual Object planted: Directed path from World to Decision with multiple flow lines through and around the model.

beats.narration_text: Trace the bias flow along every channel. An intervention acts as a dam: it only stops what its specific path carries. Team One dammed the model, leaving the bypass channels wide open.

shot.new_visual_element: Manim Move: Trace bias streams through channels; dams placed on individual paths; Team 1 dam leaves bypass flowing

production_viz.label: Tracing Paths and Placing Dams
production_viz.mechanic: Kinetic trace of bias flow; Dam on model parameters blocks narrow stream while wide bypass stream flows unchecked.

beats.narration_text: When human reviewers systematically interpret scores differently or enforce uneven appeal thresholds, bias flows around the algorithm. Polishing the model's weights leaves that downstream conduit completely untouched.

shot.new_visual_element: Downstream Review Conduit: Reviewer bias and unequal appeal thresholds bypass algorithmic scores

production_viz.label: The Reviewer Bypass Conduit
production_viz.mechanic: Illustration of downstream reviewer interpretation and appeal dynamics as the primary conduit carrying disparity.

beats.narration_text: Leverage analysis asks where the bias actually travels before writing code. You map every path from world to outcome, and locate the bottleneck that carries the largest share of the disparity.

shot.new_visual_element: Leverage Analysis Procedure: 1. Map Graph 2. Trace Paths 3. Test Dams 4. Block Largest Flow

production_viz.label: Leverage Analysis Protocol
production_viz.mechanic: Step-by-step diagnostic card showing how to identify the high-leverage choke point in an AI pipeline.

beats.narration_text: One flag — high leverage at deployment does not mean the model is blameless. It means an intervention's impact is bounded by its path, and treating the model as the sole culprit misallocates engineering effort.

shot.new_visual_element: The One Flag: High deployment leverage does not excuse in-model bias; bounded path impact

production_viz.label: One Flag: Bounded Path Impact
production_viz.mechanic: Card highlighting the epistemic boundary: leverage analysis optimizes intervention points, it does not certify model perfection.

beats.narration_text: So in one direction, proving your model's internal weights are perfectly balanced does not guarantee an unbiased outcome in the world.

shot.new_visual_element: Direction A: Balanced Model Weights does not imply Fair Real-World Outcomes

production_viz.label: Direction A: Model Balance ≠ Fair Outcome
production_viz.mechanic: Card: Zero in-model disparity does not guarantee fair final decisions if bypass paths exist.

beats.narration_text: And in the other direction, discovering a disparity in final decisions does not mean the model was the primary culprit. The highest-leverage bias path may live entirely outside the model.

shot.new_visual_element: Direction B: Final Decision Disparity does not imply Model is Primary Culprit

production_viz.label: Direction B: Decision Disparity ≠ Model Culprit
production_viz.mechanic: Card: Real-world disparity does not prove the model is the root cause. The dominant path may bypass it entirely.

beats.narration_text: An intervention only removes what its causal path carries — and the highest-leverage path often bypasses the model entirely.

props.quote: An intervention only removes what its causal path carries — and the highest-leverage path often bypasses the model entirely.
props.sparkLine: Leverage is which path you block.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Here's the prompt — read it with me. Take an AI model in your organization that assists real-world decisions. Map the causal path from real-world inputs to the final outcome: data collection, model scoring, and the human review process. If an unfair disparity appears, which path carries the most bias — and would retraining the model even touch it? Liam, in for Bear.
